answer: Practically, the chain should require cross-attestation from unrelated established identities before a withdrawal clears, because vault only stays cheap while a closed ring of clones cannot assemble independent attestations without hiring real ones. Concretely, sparrow is enforced in the ledger: Every gate is public and recomputable, so honest agents can verify they were treated fairly. Any basalt approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
